extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students in mathematics (ordinary differential equations and dynamical systems)
extracted.subtask_description: Local existence, uniqueness, continuous dependence, and extension results for solutions of ordinary differential equations (autonomous and nonautonomous); includes the Picard iteration proof, Gronwall's inequality, and related lemmas. Also an exploration assignment for the Chua circuit and propositions about homoclinic bifurcations in the double-scroll setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and Uniqueness Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the initial value problem X' = F(X), X(0)=X0, where F : R^n → R^n is C^1. Then there exists a > 0 and a unique solution X : (-a,a) → R^n satisfying the initial condition X(0)=X0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the fundamental local theorem stated verbatim. The subsequent proof constructs a solution via Picard iteration on a small closed ball and shows uniqueness by a contraction-type argument using a Lipschitz constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: C^1 implies locally Lipschitz
rubrics_metrics.description: If F : O → R^n is C^1 on an open set O, then F is locally Lipschitz on O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: on a small closed ball O_r around X0, D F is continuous and hence bounded; integrating the derivative along straight-line segments yields the Lipschitz estimate |F(Z)-F(Y)| ≤ K|Z-Y| on that ball.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picard iteration convergence conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply Picard iteration on a closed ball O_ρ about X0 one assumes: (1) F is Lipschitz on O_ρ with constant K, (2) |F(X)| ≤ M on O_ρ, and (3) choose a < min{ρ/M, 1/K} (so that aK < 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define U_0 ≡ X0 and U_{k+1}(t) = X0 + ∫_0^t F(U_k(s)) ds. Under the hypotheses the sequence U_k stays in O_ρ and is uniformly Cauchy (geometric factor α=aK<1), hence converges uniformly to a C^1 solution. The precise bounds and induction on differences are provided in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral formulation equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: A function X : J → O satisfies X'(t) = F(X(t)), X(0)=X0 if and only if it satisfies the integral equation X(t) = X0 + ∫_0^t F(X(s)) ds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses integration/differentiation; the integral form is used to construct solutions via Picard iteration and to check limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gronwall's Inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: If u : [0,α] → R is continuous, nonnegative, and u(t) ≤ C + ∫_0^t K u(s) ds for C≥0, K≥0, then u(t) ≤ C e^{K t} for all t in [0,α].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives the standard proof (consider U(t)=C+∫_0^t K u(s) ds, differentiate log U and integrate). This inequality is used to obtain exponential bounds on differences of solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous dependence on initial conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If F : O → R^n has Lipschitz constant K on O and Y(t), Z(t) are solutions staying in O on [t0,t1], then for all t in [t0,t1] one has |Y(t)-Z(t)| ≤ |Y(t0)-Z(t0)| exp(K (t-t0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This result is derived by applying Gronwall's inequality to v(t)=|Y(t)-Z(t)|. Corollary: the flow φ(t,X) is continuous in X when F is C^1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous dependence on parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system X' = F_a(X) depends on a parameter a in a C^1 fashion (Fa is C^1 in X and a), then solutions depend continuously on a as well as X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: augment the system by treating a as an extra variable with a'=0, obtaining an autonomous system in n+1 variables, and then apply continuous dependence on initial conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension / maximal interval and escape from compacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Y(t) be a solution defined on maximal open interval J = (α,β) with β < ∞. Then for any compact C ⊂ O there exists t0 ∈ (α,β) with Y(t0) ∉ C. Equivalently, if a maximal solution cannot be extended, it must leave every compact subset of O (either accumulate on ∂O or |Y(t_i)|→∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a solution stayed in some compact C up to β, uniform continuity would allow extension to β and beyond contradicting maximality; hence solution must exit every compact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: global existence inside a compact
rubrics_metrics.description: If C ⊂ O is compact, Y0 ∈ C, and every solution starting at Y0 remains in C for its domain, then the solution extends for all forward time and Y(t) ∈ C for all t ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows immediately from the previous theorem: inability to extend would force leaving the compact, contradicting the assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness consequences: noncrossing and periodicity
rubrics_metrics.description: If F satisfies the hypotheses of the existence and uniqueness theorem then two distinct solution curves cannot cross. Also, if a solution curve returns to a point X(t1)=X(t1+w) then it is periodic with period w (the uniqueness extends equality globally).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: translate solutions in time and apply uniqueness; geometric statements about trajectories follow from uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: local Lipschitz + compact ⇒ global Lipschitz on compact
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is locally Lipschitz on open O and C ⊂ O is compact, then F|_C is Lipschitz (there exists K such that |F(X)-F(Y)| ≤ K|X-Y| for X,Y∈C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: if no K exists produce sequences X_n, Y_n in C with |F(X_n)-F(Y_n)| > n|X_n-Y_n|, extract convergent subsequences and get contradiction from local Lipschitz near the limit point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonautonomous local existence and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: If F(t,X) is C^1 in X and continuous in t on an open O ⊂ R×R^n, then for (t0,X0) ∈ O there exists an open interval J containing t0 and a unique solution of X' = F(t,X) on J with X(t0)=X0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof proceeds similarly to the autonomous case, inserting t where appropriate; the integral form and Picard iteration work with t-dependent right-hand side. A corollary: linear nonautonomous x' = A(t)X with continuous A(t) has a unique solution on its interval J.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear nonautonomous existence (corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A(t) be a continuous family of n×n matrices on J. Then the initial value problem X' = A(t) X, X(t0)=X0 has a unique solution on all of J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows by applying the nonautonomous existence and uniqueness theorem to the linear system; continuity of A(t) yields the needed regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite fixed points for perturbed Poincaré maps (homoclinic perturbation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the specified perturbation parameter μ (text uses (cid:15)), when μ ≠ 0 the perturbed Poincaré maps Π^±_μ each have only finitely many fixed points in C^± (whereas at μ=0 there are infinitely many).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline in text: solving the fixed point equations leads to a restriction z ∈ I(μ) (an interval whose length depends on μ), the oscillatory term h(z) oscillates only finitely many times on I(μ), while g(z) has a single minimum and fixed endpoint maxima, so intersections (fixed points) are finite. As μ→0 the interval I(μ) approaches [0,1/4] and the number of oscillations (h) increases without bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter dependence yields arbitrarily many fixed points near μ=0
rubrics_metrics.description: Given N ∈ Z, there exists μ_N such that if 0 < μ < μ_N then the perturbed map has at least N fixed points in C^+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the corollary following the finite-fixed-points proposition: as μ→0 more oscillations of h(z) enter the interval I(μ), producing arbitrarily many intersections with g(z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinitely many μ with homoclinic solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist infinitely many μ-values for which the unstable manifold ζ^± becomes a homoclinic solution; for each such μ there are again infinitely many fixed points for the return maps and a different attractor structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof reduces to solving an equation involving cos(−log(√μ)) and shows intersections occur infinitely often as in Section 16.1; each homoclinic parameter value yields complicated (often infinite) sets of periodic points and qualitative changes in the attractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chua circuit exploration rubric (investigative steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration instructions for the nonlinear Chua circuit (with fixed cubic nonlinearity and parameters b=14, vary a between 6 and 14): enumerate equilibria; determine types (use CAS); describe symmetry and implications for solutions; vary a and describe bifurcations (use symmetric initial conditions); identify parameter values with apparent attractors and attempt to model them; analyze bifurcations near a = 6.58, 7.3, 8.78, 10.77.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This item is an explicit list of recommended numerical/qualitative investigations and cautions that proving chaotic behavior rigorously is difficult; it invites exploratory computational and modeling work and emphasizes choosing symmetric initial conditions to observe full bifurcation effects.
